description: We are NextGen Galaxy from Bangladesh, building SpaceRisk—an Earth‑observation platform using NASA satellite data to reveal environmental trends before infrastructure projects. By tracking vegetation, water, land, and urban change, we guide site selection and invite collaborators in GIS, ML, and Earthdata.
summary:
.SpaceRisk is an Earth-observation-powered infrastructure location intelligence platform that helps organizations evaluate environmental trends before investing in construction projects. Users select or draw potential sites for warehouses, factories, solar farms, telecom towers, logistics hubs, or data centers. SpaceRisk analyzes how each location has changed over time by examining vegetation condition, surface-water signals, built-up expansion, and land-surface environmental trends.

Using NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) data, SpaceRisk transforms satellite observations into understandable site-comparison insights. Instead of only showing what a location looks like today, the platform helps users explore what has changed, identify environmental trade-offs, and compare candidate sites before making expensive infrastructure decisions.

Our initial focus is Bangladesh, where rapid urban development, changing land use, heat, and water-related environmental conditions can strongly affect long-term infrastructure planning. SpaceRisk supports early-stage screening and decision-making; it is not a certified engineering, hydrological, insurance, or regulatory assessment.

SpaceRisk — Before You Build. Know the Risk.
details:
SpaceRisk is an Earth-observation-powered platform that helps businesses and organizations evaluate potential locations before investing in infrastructure development. Using NASA’s Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) satellite data, the platform analyzes historical environmental changes, including vegetation conditions, surface-water patterns, built-up area expansion, and surrounding environmental trends.

Users can select or draw a potential site and explore environmental information to understand how the area has changed over time. By turning satellite observations into understandable location insights, SpaceRisk aims to help users compare potential sites, identify environmental concerns, and make more informed infrastructure planning decisions.

The project’s main benefits include improving access to satellite-based environmental information, supporting early-stage site screening, reducing uncertainty in location selection, and encouraging more sustainable infrastructure development. Our intended impact is to make environmental intelligence more accessible and useful for businesses, planners, and decision-makers, particularly in Bangladesh, where environmental changes can significantly affect infrastructure planning.

Tools and Technologies Used:

  • Satellite Data: NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS)
  • Mobile Application: Flutter and Dart
  • Backend Development: Python and Django
  • AI-Assisted Development: ChatGPT and Google Gemini

SpaceRisk is creative because it connects satellite-based Earth observation with practical infrastructure decision-making. Rather than simply displaying satellite images, it aims to transform environmental observations into meaningful insights that people can use when evaluating potential development locations.

During development, our team considered satellite data availability, historical environmental changes, usability, accessibility, the needs of infrastructure developers, and the importance of sustainable land-use planning. We also considered the limitations of satellite-based analysis. SpaceRisk is designed as an early-stage environmental screening and decision-support platform, not a replacement for professional engineering assessments or regulatory evaluations.

SpaceRisk — Before You Build. Know the Risk.
